Thirty-one comments

A delightful easy-going tune which appears on Sharon Shannon’s CD of the same name. I believe it was written by Stephen Cooney, who plays guitar with Sharon.

I’ve submitted it in Emaj, which is the key Sharon plays it in on the CD.

The Chords - In E

Well I play in DADGAD so bear that in mind with the chords given. I am capoed on the second fret so am playing D shapes but have displayed the chords below in the key of E.

X: 1
T: Each Little Thing
M: 6/8
L: 1/8
R: jig
Z: “domnull”
Z: chords by Alistair Cassidy
K: Emaj
“E”B, | C>E“B7”F G“E”B2- | B2E F>GB | “A”ce2- e2f | e>dc “E/G#”B3- |
B2c “B7”B>GF | “E”G3-G2 B, | C>“B7”EF G“E”B2- | B2E F>GB |
“A”ce2- e2f | e>dc “E”B3- | B2G “B7”F>EE “E”E3-E2 :|
b | g>“B7”fe g2 “E”g- | g2b g>“B7”fe | “C#m”[B3e3-] e2B | c>eg “B7”f3- |
f2g f>eB | “A”c e2- e2f | e>dc B “E”e2- | e2c B>GF |
“C#m”G3- G2B | G>FE “B7”C F2- | F2“E”G “B7”F>EE | “E”E3-E2 :|

The B7 chords a lot of the time are just really runs to match the tune running down the D string 6-4-2 (or including the capo 4-2-0). They are not really meant as full chords.

BTW If you go on to become a famous musician and make fortunes out of this arrangement I want my cut!!!!

P.S. Listen to the Midi of my arrangement - it is hilarious, particualarly the pause it throws in before the second part!

↳ Posted by Jansen Wendell on February 17th, 2014.

Re: Each Little Thing

I heard it as 3/4. To me, there’s an slow underlying 1 - 2 - 3 beat. Not a waltz, of course. It never occurred to me it could be a march but I can see the logic now.

↳ Posted by DavidT on October 5th, 2016.

Each Little Thing, X:5

The previous settings have the bar lines in the wrong place - they go where the chords go, on the strong beat. So it is not a jig but a slow march in 3/4 time. I have kept it in 9/8 because that seems to give the swing better (I did try to make it 3/4 - aagh!). It is of course NOT a slip jig either - just another one of those “airs”.

↳ Posted by BelindaH on February 14th, 2017.

Re: Each Little Thing

The time should be “M:9/8”, won’t let me change it here. And I don’t know what those slur lines are doing, I didn’t put them there!

↳ Posted by BelindaH on February 14th, 2017.

Re: Each Little Thing

Thank you BelindaH! It all makes much more sense with the time signature corrected to 9/8. The slur lines are put there by abc to indicate the joined notes shown in the notation. The other option is to show it as a waltz which is kind of how Sharon Shannon plays it.

Each Little Thing, X:6 - As a waltz!

I have done anything clever. I heard this tune as a waltz and it helps me to learn it as a waltz even if, strictly, it’s not.
I’ve taken Felefeber’s version in E, transposed it down to D to play it in a session, and pasted into the Session.
